messages:
ryan: Quick sync — we need to finalize SLO + error budget allocation for the 'fast-responses' initiative before EOD Fri. Acme asked for tighter latency SLA; perf team has tradeoffs. Proposing draft below.

alex: For Hosted API I'd propose a p95 latency SLO of 200ms and availability 99.9%. Keep p50/p90 internal.

kevin: 99.9% availability feels OK for self-serve. Dedicated/enterprise should get 99.99. Also if we target p95=200ms we need KV prefill + smaller batch windows.

maya: Acme is requesting 100ms p90 + 99.95% SLA. That's only realistic if we limit to Dedicated + region pinning. Need to negotiate scope.

sarah: Graceful degrade ideas: 1) stream partial tokens immediately when tail latency spikes, 2) fall back to quantized model variant for a percentage of traffic, 3) reduce max tokens for non-enterprise plans.

ryan: Draft acceptance criteria and canary plan: please review.

ryan: ```
SLO: fast-responses-p95
target: p95 < 200ms
window: 30d
availability_target: 99.9%
error_budget: 0.1% (30d)
fallback_policy:
  - if p95 > 200ms for 10m -> route 20% traffic to fast-quantized model
  - if error_rate > 0.5% -> enable reduced-token responses for non-enterprise
canary: start 1% -> 5% over 2h; monitor burn-rate and latency
rollout_rollback: auto rollback if burn-rate > 2x expected in 1h
telemetry_tags: [feature=fast-responses, experiment=true]
```

alex: Error budget 0.1% is super tight — we should consider 0.5% to avoid constant rollbacks.

kevin: I agree with alex. Also we should consider splitting error budget: latency-burn and availability-burn separate so we don't conflate.

maya: For enterprise SLA path: propose we offer 99.95% + p90 120ms but only on Dedicated with reserved capacity and region pinning. I'll confirm with Acme.

sarah: Acceptance checklist (quick):
- SLO config in metrics pipeline
- Canary config and automations
- Runbooks + alert thresholds for burn-rate
- Fallback deploy tested in staging
- Customer scope doc for SLA

alex: Engineering action items: prototype fallback routing (alex+kevin), run perf tests with prefill, simulate burst cache misses.

kevin: Prioritization note: tuning batching and KV-prefill reduces cost per token and addresses tail latency better than micro-optimizing kernels. Recommend #1 batching tweaks, #2 KV prefill, #3 model quantization.

ryan: PM action items: 1) @maya negotiate SLA scope w/ Acme, 2) finalize SLO targets and error budget split, 3) confirm signoff criteria for launch.

maya: pinging Acme CSM now, will paste convo here when I have clarity.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: fast-responses v1 -> traffic=1%

alex: Add automatic rollback if error budget burn-rate > 2x in a 1-hour window. Also tag traces with "experiment=fast-responses".

kevin: +1 to rollback. Also add a metric for cache-miss tail latency and set a separate alert.

ryan: Sounds good. Target to finalize today so SRE can create runbooks tomorrow. If Acme insists on 100ms p90 we'll scope to Dedicated only.

maya: Update: Acme replied — willing to accept Dedicated-only SLA. They want a firm launch date before end of quarter.

deploy-bot: Canary status update: traffic=5%, errors stable, p95=185ms

sarah: :thumbsup:

ryan: Thanks all — I'll compile these notes into a short PRD + SLO RFC and tag reviewers. If anyone has objections to the 200ms p95/0.5% error budget split (latency/availability) speak now.

alex: No objections from eng, prefer 0.5% error budget.

kevin: No objections.

maya: Will finalize customer-facing SLA terms today and upload the addendum.

ryan: Closing thread — next steps in PRD doc. Thanks.
